title: Vanishing for sheaves supported on closed points
statement:
Let $K$ be a separably closed
field and $X$ a scheme of finite type over $K$. Let $F$ be an
abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$ whose support
is contained in the set of
closed points of $X$. Then
$H^q(X_{\Et},F)=0$ for $q>0$. (*Source:* Stacks Project,
Tag [0F1F](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F1F), first
assertion.)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to $X\to\operatorname{Spec}K$: a field is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $K$), so $X$ is Noetherian, hence locally Noetherian and quasi-compact. By [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], $X$ is also quasi-separated. These are precisely the hypotheses on the scheme in the filtered-colimit cohomology theorem used in Step 7.

source.place: Tag 0F1F, lemma-supported-in-closed-points, proof of the vanishing assertion; Tag 01T6, morphisms-lemma-finite-type-noetherian; Tag 01OY, properties-lemma-locally-Noetherian-quasi-separated

proof.text: By [lem-kun-cp-approximation], write $F=\varinjlim_{a\in A}F_a$ as the filtered colimit of its finitely generated subsheaves. Each $F_a$ has support a finite set $Z_a$ of closed points. Here $A$ is the directed set of these subsheaves, ordered by inclusion: the zero subsheaf supplies an element and the sum of two finitely generated subsheaves is generated by the union of their finite lists of generators. Take subsheaves in the fixed site universe, so $A$ is a set. For the reduced closed subscheme with underlying set $Z_a$, write $i_a:Z_a\hookrightarrow X$. The approximation theorem gives $F_a\cong i_{a,*}G_a$, with $G_a=F_a|_{Z_a}$; this also follows directly from [lem-kun-04ca], since the support of $F_a$ is contained in $Z_a$.

source.place: Tag 0F1F, lemma-supported-in-closed-points, proof of the vanishing assertion; Tag 0F0N, lemma-support-in-subset, specialized to closed points; Tag 04CA, proposition-closed-immersion-pushforward

proof.text: Fix $a$. The finite space $Z_a$ is discrete: for each $z\in Z_a$, its complement is a finite union of closed singletons. Thus the singleton open subschemes form a finite clopen decomposition of $Z_a$. Each singleton open subscheme is affine, since any affine neighbourhood of its point is the whole singleton. Write it as $\operatorname{Spec}B_z$. The ring $B_z$ is reduced by [def-pc-reduced-scheme] and has just one prime ideal. That ideal is both maximal and the nilradical, hence zero; consequently $B_z$ is a field. On this singleton scheme the local ring at $z$ is $B_z$. The closed-immersion definition [def-weil-closed-immersion] gives a surjective local homomorphism $\mathcal O_{X,z}\twoheadrightarrow B_z$ on stalks. Since $B_z$ is a field, its kernel is the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_{X,z}$; hence $B_z\cong\mathcal O_{X,z}/\mathfrak m_{X,z}=\kappa_X(z)$ by [def-weil-residue-field]. Therefore $Z_a\cong\coprod_{z\in Z_a}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa_X(z)$. This argument includes $Z_a=\varnothing$, with an empty coproduct.

source.place: Tag 0F1F, lemma-supported-in-closed-points, proof of the vanishing assertion

proof.text: For every $z\in Z_a$, [lem-kun-closed-point-field] (b) applies to the original finite-type $K$-scheme $X$: $\kappa_X(z)$ is a finite purely inseparable extension of $K$ and is itself separably closed. Apply [lem-kun-03qu-sep-closed] to the restriction of $G_a$ to each $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa_X(z)$. The finite clopen product formula [lem-weil-pbc-finite-coproduct-cohomology-assembly] now gives, for $q>0$, $H^q((Z_a)_{\Et},G_a)\cong\prod_{z\in Z_a}H^q(\operatorname{Spec}\kappa_X(z)_{\Et},G_a|_z)=0$. The empty product in abelian groups is the zero group.

source.place: Tag 0F1F, lemma-supported-in-closed-points, proof of the vanishing assertion; Tag 03QU, lemma-compare-cohomology-point; finite clopen assembly as used in Tag 0A5B, lemma-constant-smooth-statements

proof.text: The closed immersion $i_a$ is finite. Indeed, [def-weil-closed-immersion] identifies its inverse image over every affine $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq X$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(R/J)$ for an ideal $J$. The $R$-module $R/J$ is generated by $1$, so the affine-local definition [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] of a finite morphism applies.

source.place: Tag 0F1F, lemma-supported-in-closed-points, proof of the vanishing assertion; Tag 01QO, morphisms-lemma-closed-immersion; Tag 01WH, morphisms-definition-integral

proof.text: By [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact], $i_{a,*}$ is exact and $Ri_{a,*}G_a\cong i_{a,*}G_a\cong F_a$ when these sheaves are regarded as complexes in degree zero. Such complexes are bounded below. Applying [lem-kun-leray-bdd] to $i_a$ therefore yields $R\Gamma((Z_a)_{\Et},G_a)\cong R\Gamma(X_{\Et},F_a)$. Taking degree-$q$ cohomology, as in [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], and using Step 4 gives $H^q(X_{\Et},F_a)=0$ for every $q>0$.

source.place: Tag 0F1F, lemma-supported-in-closed-points, proof of the vanishing assertion; Tag 03QP, proposition-finite-higher-direct-image-zero, and the Leray comparison used in Tag 0F1F

proof.text: The scheme $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by Step 1 and $(F_a)_{a\in A}$ is a set-indexed filtered system of abelian etale sheaves by Step 2. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-filtered-colimit] applies without any torsion hypothesis and gives $H^q(X_{\Et},F)\cong\varinjlim_{a\in A}H^q(X_{\Et},F_a)$. For $q>0$ every term is zero by Step 6, so this colimit is zero. This proves the assertion for the original arbitrary abelian sheaf $F$.
